summary: Ice surface of each year 2016 to 2026 on the 3D strip: two swisstopo elevation models (2015, 2023), swisstopo lidar (26 tiles of 2021) and an elevation-band lowering shape borrowed from Corbassiere for the years between and beyond. A model, not a measurement, except where a survey lies.

anchors.survey: GLAMOS volume-change table (release 2025, all-combinations file) lists this surface as source "sa3d-2018" with date_end 20159999: survey 2015, day unknown. Image strips over the strip in 2015 (swisstopo layer ch.swisstopo.lubis-bildstreifen): 2015-08-26 TLM (100 % of ice cells, computed), 2015-09-20 TLM (74 % of ice cells, computed), 2015-09-21 TLM (100 % of ice cells, computed). Which strip fed which cell is not published; the model puts the whole edition on one day.
anchors.placed_at: 2015-09-21 (a day a strip was flown, taken from the pair of flown days with the lowest ICESat-2 rmse (1.38 m); ties within 0.05 m go to the GLAMOS date if it is among them, else to the strip covering most ice. Chosen on the same shots as the check, so not independent)

anchors.source: swissSURFACE3D raster (swisstopo lidar DSM, 0.5 m, read at 20 m)
anchors.survey: GPS times of the point clouds of 26 tiles read (tiles with ice). 18 tiles hold at least 85 % of their points on a single day (2021-09-22 on 12, 2021-08-24 on 6); 8 tiles were flown on several days within 60 days and take the point-weighted mean day (uncertain by up to about a month); 0 tiles flown on days further apart (or not read) are not used. The lidar sits on 100 % of the ice cells (computed).
anchors.placed_at: the flight day of each tile (see above)

anchors.survey: Built from aerial images 2023: strips over the ice 2023-08-23 SWISSIMAGE (13 % of ice cells, computed), 2023-09-06 SWISSIMAGE (100 % of ice cells, computed). GLAMOS names 20230823 (is-stand). Which strip fed which cell is not published.
anchors.placed_at: 2023-09-06 (a day a strip was flown, chosen with A1 by the same pair rule)

shape: Between two anchors the surface follows the lowering of each elevation band, from snow-off (1 May plus Bw/|Bs| x 153 d, melt even from 1 May: an assumption) to 30 September. GLAMOS has no band balance for Feegletscher (no row in the elevation-bin file; no point file of the annual, winter or intermediate sets). The band balance is that of Corbassiere (release 2025, bins from 2200 to 4400 m covering 100 % of the ice, computed; non-commercial); it only decides how the change between two surveys is spread, the size comes from the surveys. Tried on the same ICESat-2 shots (rmse, computed): Corbassiere 1.39 m; Findel 1.46 m (covers 97 %: not eligible); the borrowed line 2.32 m (covers 84 %: not eligible); Aletsch 2.66 m; Rhone 3.37 m (covers 91 %: not eligible); the lowest among the candidates covering at least 98 % of the ice is used. 2026: the Corbassiere bands are estimated (computed): each band regressed on the glacier-wide Bw and Bs of Grosser Aletsch (2005 to 2025) and evaluated at the Aletsch 2026 values read from the GLAMOS figure (Bw +751.6, Bs -3790.0 mm w.e., about +-100 mm w.e.). Beyond the last anchor (2024 to 2026) the rate of the last segment is applied to the measured 2023 surface, from the anchor difference smoothed over about 100 m (the raw difference carries noise and made 2024 to 2026 rough). The ground outside the 2023 outline stays at its 2023 height and no fade is applied, so a step grows along the outline (median lowering of the ice cells next to it 1.1 m in 2024, 2.0 m in 2025, 3.7 m in 2026, computed). Every cell stays between its two anchors or, outside them, within 2.5 times the lowering of its band at the nearest anchor.

validation.icesat2: ICESat-2 ATL06 v007: 697 shots on 2023 ice in 4 granules (July to October, slope under 20 degrees, quality 0, h_li_sigma under 1 m, inside the physical envelope). rmse 1.38 m over all years, bias −0.02 m (model minus shot), leave-one-granule-out: the A1 and A2 days are chosen on the other granules and the held-out granule is scored; with the days used 1.39 m. Per year (leave-one-granule-out): 2019 1.21 m (275 shots); 2021 1.31 m (47 shots); 2025 1.50 m (375 shots). Years without summer shots are not checked.
validation.datum: Heights are corrected with a plane fitted on 7230 shots on stable ground outside the ice (NMAD 1.45 m).
validation.not_checked: The split of the loss between years is an assumption (even melt from snow-off to 30 September); ICESat-2 scores years with shots, not each year step. 9 of 86 ASTER AST14DEM scenes (NASA LP DAAC, July to October 2016 to 2026) passed the gate (rock NMAD at most 15 m, at least 300 rock and 200 ice cells) in 2016, 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021; ASTER is rough, so only differences of a few metres mean something. No stake check: GLAMOS has no point mass balance for Feegletscher (release 2025: no file of the annual, winter or intermediate sets).

bed: Ice surfaces are not allowed below the bedrock: swissBEDROCK (swisstopo, 10 m; under glaciers swissALTI3D minus a modelled ice thickness, GLAMOS 2020) is the floor.
not_used: Airborne research DEMs and TanDEM-X series: the RAGMAC set covers Aletsch only (read); a first search for others is recorded in the source ledger of this glacier, and none was used; no radar surface was used. Years before 2016 are not modelled: older pictures use the 2016 surface.
licences: swisstopo open government data (swissALTI3D, swissSURFACE3D, image-strip footprints). The GLAMOS balances of Corbassiere and volume change: non-commercial (file headers). ICESat-2 (NASA, ATL06) and ASTER AST14DEM (NASA LP DAAC): used for checking only; the ASTER terms of use were not read. GLAMOS ice thickness release 2020 (radar beds, CC BY 4.0 per the landing page) and swissBEDROCK (swisstopo open government data): used for the ice bed checks.
caveat_2026: estimate: extrapolated like 2024-2025, with the 2026 balance of the Corbassiere bands estimated from the GLAMOS figure for Aletsch (computed regression): provisional; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots)

bed.lead: Some checks on Feegletscher (all computed here, not source figures; those that cannot be made are said so). The bed is the rock under the ice. "Radar bed" is the radar's own bed elevation (the survey surface minus the measured thickness, from the GLAMOS release); "model bed" is swissBEDROCK, which under glaciers is swissALTI3D minus a modelled GLAMOS ice thickness.
checks:
1 · Radar bed against model bed

At the 401 radar cells (20 m, median of the points in a cell), how far apart are the two beds?

Median −0.2 m over all cells (one survey, 2013). Spread (standard deviation) 5.7 m; 92 % are within 10 m and 100 % within 30 m.

Reading: 92 % of the cells of the 2013 survey lie within 10 m. This is not a validation: the model bed was made from these same surveys (GLAMOS 2020 model, Grab et al. 2021), and at the survey lines it is the measured bed.

2 · One survey against another

Where two surveys covered the same spot, how well do they repeat?

Cannot be checked: no spot of the strip has two survey dates in the GLAMOS radar data.

3 · Ground that is ice free now

Radar points where the newest swissALTI3D shows ground, not ice: the exposed ground is the bed.

Cannot be checked: no radar point lies in ground that is ice free now, at least 30 m outside the SGI2023 outline and 30 m inside the SGI2016 outline.

notes.uncertainty: Median over the ice of 2023, red whisker the 90th percentile (computed). The two swisstopo surveys carry 1.22 m (rmse of the 275 shots of 2019, the year with the lowest rmse among those with at least 100 shots; there are no usable shots in 2023, so this is an upper bound). The lidar of 2021 carries 1.00 m (rmse of 43 shots within 45 days of the lidar day). swisstopo quotes 0.5 m below 2000 m and 1 to 3 m above (as quoted by Bannwart et al.), so the true value may be larger on a tongue this high. Between and beyond the surveys the error grows with the size of the change (factors 1.17 and 0.17), calibrated on the same ICESat-2 shots, so it is not independent; where a year has shots it is not below their rmse. Years without shots (2016, 2017, 2018, 2020, 2022, 2023, 2024) rest on the formula alone. 2026 has no value on the chart: it is an estimate (its balance is estimated from a figure for Aletsch), and its map in the viewer adds 25 % of its increment (median 1.8 m).
notes.sharing: Solid: the loss between two surveys is shared over the years by an elevation-band balance borrowed from Corbassiere (GLAMOS has none for Feegletscher; chosen on ICESat-2 among the candidates that cover the ice). Dashed: extrapolated beyond the last survey (2026 with an estimated balance). Not used: measured years.
notes.independent: ICESat-2 also chose the survey days of both anchors and calibrated σ, so it is not independent (rmse is leave-one-granule-out). ASTER scenes are checks only (9 of 86 scenes usable; usable years: 2016, 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021). There are no stake readings for Feegletscher after its first survey. Click a year for the numbers.

page.viewerText: The yearly surfaces in 3D with a year slider, the same viewer as for Aletsch. Switch on ICESat-2 shots (what the model was checked against) and hover a shot for its values; the bed and uncertainty colours are in the Colour menu. About 5 MB, loaded when you press the button.
page.mapcap: The model area = the 3D strip (outlined in black), as set in the walkthrough. Blue: ice inside the 2023 outline, about 13.1 km² (computed, 20 m cells). Red dashed: every cell modelled as ice, including ground that was ice at the 2015 survey, about 14.3 km² (computed). The 697 ICESat-2 shots used for the checks are shown in the 3D viewer (last section). The ICESat-2 check covers the cells within 1 km of a shot; the rest, 2 % of the modelled ice cells (656 of 31,678, computed), follows the same rules but has no check. Pictures of years before 2016 use the 2016 surface.
page.icesatNote: Also used to choose the survey days of both anchors, so not an independent check; the rmse is leave-one-granule-out (the days are chosen on the other granules).
page.asterNote: For scale: each used scene has a stable-terrain NMAD of 8.8 to 15.0 m (computed) (no used scene lies within 25 days of the 2023 anchor), so differences of a few metres are within ASTER's own scatter. rms = spread of the scene values of the year. Check only, not in the fit.
